en.name: Threadfin
en.summary: Threadfin — 午仔魚 in Taiwan — is a fine-textured fish farmed fat enough to sit on the oily side of the line. Fresh, it keeps 1–2 days in the fridge and 2–3 months in the freezer. The salted, part-dried version is a different food with a different life.
en.pantry: Fresh threadfin has no room-temperature life. Farmed fish of this kind carries enough fat to go rancid quickly and enough moisture to spoil quickly, so the trip home is where most of the damage is done. Take a cool bag, follow the 2-hour rule, and 1 hour if the market is above 32 °C (90 °F). The salted 一夜干 style — split, brined and dried overnight — is a separate product and should not be judged by these figures.
en.fridge: Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, gutted, on ice, in a container that catches the melt water, and cook it within 1–2 days. Have the stall gut and scale it: threadfin has soft flesh and the guts are where spoilage starts. Store it on the bottom shelf, below ready-to-eat food, and pat it dry before it goes in so it is not sitting in liquid. A whole fish holds up better than butterflied fillets, which are what most Taiwanese shoppers actually buy.
en.freezer: Threadfin keeps 2–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — the shorter of the two fish windows, because it is an oily fish and fat oxidises in the freezer long before lean flesh does. Wrap it tightly with no air pockets, or ice-glaze it by dipping in cold water first, and freeze flat in single portions. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are a quality window, and an oily fish kept past it tastes unmistakably of old oil.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight on a plate, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never on the counter or in warm water. Cook it promptly and do not refreeze raw fish.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell instead of a clean sea one.
Flesh that stays dented when pressed rather than springing back.
Cloudy sunken eyes and grey-brown gills on a whole fish.
A rancid, paint-like smell and a yellow cast on the belly flesh.
tips: Have it gutted and scaled at the stall.
Buy whole rather than butterflied if you are not cooking today.
Freeze in single portions the day you buy it.
Do not apply these numbers to the salted, part-dried version.

faq.q: How long does fresh threadfin keep?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, gutted and on ice. Frozen, 2–3 months at −18 °C.
Yes, 2–3 months at −18 °C. Wrap it airtight or ice-glaze it; the window is short because it is an oily fish.

faq.q: Is salted threadfin the same thing?
faq.a: No. The salted, part-dried style is a different product with a different shelf life, and these figures do not apply to it.

faq.q: How can you tell if threadfin has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, a rancid note from the belly, flesh that will not spring back, or dull sunken eyes.

zh.name: 午仔魚
zh.summary: 午仔魚肉質細緻，台灣的養殖個體油脂夠多，屬於偏油的那一類。新鮮的冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 2～3 個月。鹽漬半乾的一夜干是另一種食物，保存方式也不同。
zh.pantry: 新鮮午仔魚沒有室溫保存這回事。這類養殖魚脂肪多到很快會油耗、水分也多到很快會腐敗，所以回家那段路往往就是損傷最大的地方。請帶保冷袋，並守 2 小時原則，市場溫度超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。剖開鹽漬、風乾一夜的「一夜干」是另一種產品，不適用本篇的數字。
zh.fridge: 去內臟後鋪冰，放 4 °C 以下，容器要能接住融水，並在 1～2 天內煮掉。請攤商代為去鱗去內臟：午仔魚肉質軟，而腐敗是從內臟開始的。放最下層、位置低於即食食品；下冰箱前先擦乾，不要讓牠泡在水裡。整條比對剖的魚片耐放，雖然台灣消費者買的多半是對剖的。
zh.freezer: 午仔魚在 −18 °C 下可放 2～3 個月——是兩種魚類區間裡較短的那個，因為它是油脂魚，而脂肪在冷凍庫裡遠比瘦肉更早氧化。包緊不留空氣，或先浸冷水做冰鍍，分成單份壓平冷凍。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質；油脂魚放過頭，吃起來就是一股陳油味。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏隔夜解凍，或密封裝袋用冷水沖。不要放室溫或泡溫水。解凍後盡快烹調，生魚不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨的海味。
按壓後凹陷回不來，而不是有彈性。
整條魚眼睛混濁凹陷、魚鰓轉灰褐。
腹部肉泛黃並帶油耗、油漆般的氣味。
tips: 請攤商當場去鱗去內臟。
今天不煮的話買整條，不要買對剖的。
買回來當天就分成單份冷凍。
鹽漬半乾的一夜干不適用這些數字。

faq.q: 新鮮午仔魚可以放多久？
faq.a: 去內臟鋪冰、放 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。冷凍則是 −18 °C 下 2～3 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 2～3 個月。包緊或做冰鍍；因為是油脂魚，期限比較短。
不一樣。鹽漬半乾的一夜干是另一種產品，保存期限不同，本篇數字不適用。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷午仔魚不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、腹部有油耗味、按壓沒有彈性，或眼睛混濁凹陷。
